verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's entire task model is real code: tasks are 'plain async/await functions with no workflow DSL, no determinism rules' and can be triggered, chained, and awaited from within other code (triggerAndWait, trigger.trigger). This directly supports writing real code steps inside a workflow, well documented across docs and confirmed by community devs using it as an extension of their Node apps. However, evidence only covers JavaScript/TypeScript — there is no mention of native Python task support, only mention of Python in the story is unaddressed. Missing for 10: Python code-step support, hands-on independent verification of mixed-language steps within a single workflow.
